citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
On July 4, 2026 animal care staff discovered that a male Rhesus Macaque (ID RA 3150) had not received his approved
amount of water on July 3, 2026. This nonhuman primate was part of the approved IACUC protocol (2025 - 2200204) that
allows for water restriction, however the protocol was not followed and resulted in the animal not receiving its full water
ration. This animal was to receive 350 ml of water, however only 100 ml was administered. The veterinary staff was
alerted of the issue and the animal received three times its required daily water allotment. A veterinary exam revealed the
animal was not dehydrated and appeared clinically healthy.
Failure to follow the approved protocol’s directions may affect the health and well-being of the animals. The IACUC must
ensure that all activities related to the care and use of animals are reviewed and approved. As part of the corrective
action, lab members were retrained and the lab was placed on mandatory post approval monitoring. Additionally the lab
must submit daily water logs to the IACUC.
CORRECTED on 7/4/2026

citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
Pertaining to IACUC approved protocol (2025-00016), the principle investigator (PI) implemented a change to an ongoing
activity without prior review and approval from the IACUC. On 7/23/26 the IACUC was reviewing the amendment
requesting the addition of two procedures to the protocol involving gerbils. Prior to the amendment being approved, the PI
confirmed that one of the procedures had been performed.
Making unapproved changes to a protocol does not allow the IACUC time to review. By following an approved protocol,
the IACUC can ensure the animals involved do not experience negative impacts to their health and well-being. The
IACUC must ensure that all changes regarding the care and use of animals in ongoing activities are reviewed and
approved prior to implementation.
Correct by ensuring that proposed activities contain a complete and accurate description of the proposed use of the
animals and are approved by the IACUC prior to starting activities or implementing any changes.
CORRECTED ON 8/11/2026, the amendments to the protocol above were reviewed and approved.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:

APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
